newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech output revives but wages, floods worry.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech output revives but wages, floods worry.

text.p: Czech industrial output rebounded strongly in June but analysts tempered hopes that the economy was back on track with warnings of stubbornly high wages and potentially major problems caused by recent flooding.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released data on Monday showing real industrial output jumped 7.9 percent, year-on- year, in June, after contracting a real 3.3 percent the previous month. In June 1996 output rose 1.8 percent.
But the CSU data also showed nominal industrial wages were 15.9 percent higher, year-on-year, up from 11.9 percent growth in May.
"The CSU figures confirmed the growth of industrial output that was expected given forecast high industrial sales," said Jan Urban, chief analyst at Union Banka.
Industrial sales rose 10.7 percent in real terms in June.

"(But) an unfriendly fact is that growth of real wages at 8.5 percent, which is the largest rise this year...This negative trend is also prevalent in the construction sector, where real wages grew 7.9 percent," he added.
The CSU said real construction output for June contracted 2.8 percent. There was one more working day in June 1997 than in the same month last year but the bureau did not comment further on the fall.
Analysts said recent flooding in the eastern third of the country in July dampened any hopes that the uptrend in output could be sustained.

In one of the country's worst natural disasters in a century, severe flooding caused by torrential rains last month devastated parts of the east of the Czech Republic, as well as parts of western Poland, killing some 100 people.
As people return to their homes, damage estimates continue to grow. Economists have put the cost at 50-100 billion crowns and many large factories in the area are still cleaning up.
"The effects of the floods will be devatstating at some firms," said one foreign analyst. "Some major firms closed down for several weeks and this will impact heavily on July output data."
Among the larger firms affected are tyre maker Barum Continental and Skoda Automobilova, both of which are major exporters.
The Czech crown was unaffected by the data, with dealers saying the figures were as expected, adding that the quiet summer season made the near-term outlook for the currency stable.
"We didn't see any unexpected results for the economy," said Jan Strupek of Komercni Banka.
The crown traded around 18.371 against the mark in late morning after opening at 18.418. -- Prague Newsroom, +420-2-2423-0003
